patterns.usage_note: Singles out one item and denies everything else, so the predicate is always negative: 千円しかない says the amount falls short, where だけ merely counts it. It replaces が and を but stacks on に, へ, で, から, まで, と (東京にしかない). After a plain verb it also gives 行くしかない, "no choice but to", an attachment this rule does not cover.

examples.ruby: 財布[さいふ]には千円[せんえん]しか入[はい]っていなかった。
examples.english: There was only a thousand yen in my wallet.

examples.ruby: この花[はな]は高[たか]い山[やま]にしか咲[さ]かないそうだ。
examples.english: Apparently this flower blooms nowhere but high in the mountains.

examples.ruby: その店[みせ]は五時[ごじ]までしか開[あ]いていないよ。
examples.english: That place is only open till five, you know.
